nodes.summary: Counting lemma: for any family of reals `t` indexed by `G` and any `k`, at most `k` elements `h` have rank count `#{g | t h ≤ t g}` at most `k`.
nodes.title: Counting lemma for rank counts

nodes.summary: For arbitrary `A` and `B` in a finite type with `n` elements, the number of `t`-subsets that contain `A` and are disjoint from `B` is `(n - #A - #B).choose (t - #A)` when `A` and `B` are disjoint and `#A ≤ t`, and `0` otherwise.
nodes.title: Counting `t`-subsets with a prescribed inside and outside, in general

nodes.summary: In a finite type with `n` elements, if `A` and `B` are disjoint and `#A ≤ t`, the `t`-subsets that contain `A` and are disjoint from `B` number `(n - #A - #B).choose (t - #A)`. The hypothesis `#A ≤ t` is needed: without it the count is `0` while the truncated right-hand side need not be; see `card_powersetCard_filter_subset_disjoint_eq_ite`.
nodes.title: Counting `t`-subsets with a prescribed inside and outside

nodes.summary: Phipson and Smyth (2010); Hemerik and Goeman (2018): if the null law `μ` is invariant under a finite group `G` and `g₁, …, g_B` are drawn independently and uniformly from `G`, independently of the data, then `(1 + #{b | T(g_b • ω) ≥ T(ω)}) / (B + 1)` is a valid p-value under the joint law.
nodes.title: Validity of Monte Carlo permutation p-values

nodes.summary: Lehmann and Romano (2005), §15.2; Hemerik and Goeman (2018): if the law `μ` is invariant under the action of a finite group `G`, the permutation p-value of any measurable statistic is valid.
nodes.title: Validity of permutation p-values

nodes.summary: Let `n` be the number of vertices, `M` the number of edges and `1 ≤ t < n`. The average, over the `n.choose t` subsets `S` with `t` elements, of the number of edges with exactly one endpoint in `S` is `2t(n-t)/(n(n-1)) * M`.
nodes.title: Mean edge cut of a uniform `t`-subset

nodes.summary: If the law `μ` is invariant under the action of a finite group `G`, and for `μ`-almost every `ω` exactly `c` group elements `g` move `ω` into the measurable set `A`, then `μ A = c / |G|`. Summing `μ (g⁻¹ • A) = μ A` over `G` turns `|G| μ A` into the integral of the number of such `g`.
nodes.title: Averaging over an invariant finite group

nodes.summary: The Monte Carlo permutation p-value `(1 + #{b | T(g_b • ω) ≥ T(ω)}) / (B + 1)` of the statistic `T` at the data `ω` with the `B` drawn group elements `g`.
nodes.title: Monte Carlo permutation p-value

nodes.summary: The permutation (group-invariance) p-value of the statistic `T` at `ω`: the fraction of group elements `g` with `T (g • ω) ≥ T ω`.
nodes.title: Permutation p-value

nodes.summary: For `1 ≤ t`, the numbers of edges of `G` with exactly one endpoint in `S`, summed over the `t`-subsets `S` of the vertices, give `2 * M * (n - 2).choose (t - 1)`, where `M` is the number of edges and `n` the number of vertices.
nodes.title: Sum of the edge cut over all `t`-subsets

nodes.summary: Let `n ≥ 4` be the number of vertices, `M` the number of edges, `S₂ = ∑ v, (G.degree v) ^ 2` and `1 ≤ t < n`. Put `a = 2t(n-t)/(n(n-1))` and `b = 4t(t-1)(n-t)(n-t-1)/(n(n-1)(n-2)(n-3))`. For `S` uniform among the `t`-subsets, the population variance of the cut size `R S = #(G.interedges S Sᶜ)`, written as the average of `(R S - μ) ^ 2` with `μ` the average of `R`, is `b * M + (a / 2 - b) * S₂ + (b - a ^ 2) * M ^ 2`.
nodes.title: Variance of the edge cut of a uniform `t`-subset

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
